name: Chili Oil (5-min + infused upgrade)
source: Homemade; infused version adapted from Made With Lau (Cantonese)

ingredients.name: Coarse red chili flakes (pul biber / gochugaru / Kirkland)
[Infused ver, optional] Star anise (rinsed), sesame seeds, sesame oil

steps: OIL + TEMP (both versions): high-oleic canola is ideal. Pour at ~150C / 300F, NOT hotter - hot oil scorches flakes bitter (esp. seed-heavy Kirkland). Shimmering, not smoking.
== VERSION A (5-min) ==
A1. Chili flakes + pinch salt in a heatproof bowl.
A2. Heat oil to ~150C (shimmering).
A3. Pour hot oil over flakes - it sizzles. Stir. Cool, jar it.
== VERSION B (~10-min infused, RECOMMENDED) ==
B1. Heat oil to ~150C. A piece of onion should bubble gently.
B2. Fry ginger ~15s, add garlic, add onion (+ rinsed star anise if using). Stir constantly ~2.5-3 min until browned; lower heat if too hot.
B3. Fish out ALL aromatics (squeeze oil back in). Nothing fresh stays in the oil = food-safe + freezer-friendly.
B4. If oil overheated, add ~1 tbsp room-temp oil to bring back to ~150C.
B5. Pour hot oil over the chili flakes - sizzle, stir.
B6. Optional: stir in sesame seeds, then a final 1/2 tsp sesame oil for aroma. Cool, jar it.
STORAGE: fridge 3-4 weeks; freezer months (oil goes thick/cloudy, not solid - scoop straight out, leave headspace in glass).
TIP - Zero-effort cheat: skip the batch entirely, bloom a pinch of flakes in the pot with the garlic+ginger when you make the ramen.

name: Quick Miso-Chili Ramen (tantanmen-style)
source: Adapted from a FB coconut-miso recipe, tuned to authentic tantanmen
steps: Bloom aromatics: heat chili oil in the pot, add ginger + garlic, ~45 sec until fragrant.
Chicken: add the chicken, cook through (~3-4 min).
Simmer: pour in broth + soy milk + soy sauce, simmer ~3 min.
Off the heat: whisk miso + tahini into a ladle of hot broth until smooth, stir back in. Never boil miso - it flattens the aroma.
Finish: sesame oil + a few drops rice vinegar. Taste and adjust.
Cook noodles separately, drain, pour broth over.
TIP - Coconut is a Western fusion move; authentic tantanmen uses UNSWEETENED SOY MILK (dairy-free, adds protein not just fat). Almond milk = thinner backup.
TIP - Laksa fork: keep coconut milk + lime + a little curry paste for a Thai-style coconut noodle soup instead. Different dish, also good.

name: Easy Honey Lemon Garlic Glazed Salmon

ingredients.name: Salmon fillet (cut into 2 pieces if thick)

steps: Season the salmon with salt, black pepper, and paprika.
In a small bowl, mix together honey, lemon juice, soy sauce, garlic, salt and chili flakes.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Place salmon skin-side down and cook for 4 minutes until the skin is crispy. Flip and cook the other side for 2 minutes.
Pour in the glaze and let it bubble for a minute, spooning it over the salmon as it thickens and coats the fish.
Add a bit of butter at the end, stirring it through the sauce.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with extra glaze spooned over the top.
Serve with rice, roasted veggies, or a simple salad.

name: Horseradish Yogurt Sauce
steps: Stir everything together in a bowl.
Taste, adjust horseradish/salt/lemon.
Rest in fridge 15-20 min -- flavors marry, horseradish blooms.

TIP — choosing chrein: BEET chrein (red) = milder, slightly sweet, tints the sauce pink. WHITE chrein = fiery, sinus-clearing, no sweetness. Beet works great here (milder is nicer); use white if you want the punch. Base yogurt: 0% Greek for max protein (~10g P/100g), full-fat for richer texture.

name: Pot Roast (House Version)

ingredients.name: Onions, rough chopped (house swap from shallots)
Cooking fat, wine, stock (stock not bouillon)

steps: Salt the roast generously on all sides (~20g/side). Rest 20+ min while you prep veg.
Prep mirepoix: rough-chop onions, celery, carrots (obliques), crush garlic.
Sear the chuck hard on all sides -- color = flavor.
Sweat the veg in the same pot until edges catch color.
Deglaze with wine, scrape the fond, reduce.
Add stock (no bouillon), nestle the roast back in.
Braise covered in oven, low (~300F/150C), 4-4.5 hours until shreddable but holding together.
Rest 30 min before serving so the meat reabsorbs liquid.
Loaded mash: wrap 6 russets each in foil, slow-roast alongside roast ~2 hr until tender; smash with salt, 1 stick butter, a dollop of sour cream.
Plate: rip a chunk of beef onto the potatoes, spoon over veg, glaze with sauce.

name: Morning Oats (non-jump days)
steps: Cook the oats in the water.
Move to a bowl, mix in all remaining ingredients.
Finish with cracked sea salt.
